claims: Six men have achieved the modern career Golf Grand Slam by winning all four major championships (Masters, PGA Championship, U.S. Open, The Open Championship) in their careers.
Gene Sarazen, Ben Hogan, Gary Player, Jack Nicklaus, Tiger Woods, and Rory McIlroy have achieved the modern career Golf Grand Slam.
Rory McIlroy completed the modern career Golf Grand Slam at the 2025 Masters.
Jack Nicklaus and Tiger Woods achieved the Triple Crown by winning each major at least three times.
Gene Sarazen completed the feat at the 1935 Masters.
Ben Hogan completed the feat at the 1953 Open Championship.
Gary Player completed the feat at the 1965 U.S. Open.
Jack Nicklaus completed the feat at the 1966 Open Championship.
Tiger Woods completed the feat at the 2000 Open Championship.
Rory McIlroy completed the feat at the 2025 Masters.
In 2000-2001, Tiger Woods became the only player to hold all four modern major titles simultaneously.
Jack Nicklaus holds the record with 18 professional major championship victories.
Phil Mickelson lacks U.S. Open.
Jordan Spieth lacks PGA Championship.
Scottie Scheffler lacks U.S. Open.
Phil Mickelson, Jordan Spieth, and Scottie Scheffler have each won three of the four majors.
The women's Career Grand Slam has varied over time regarding which tournaments constitute the four majors.
Mickey Wright is a Women's Career Grand Slam Winner (Modern).
Pat Bradley is a Women's Career Grand Slam Winner (Modern).
Juli Inkster is a Women's Career Grand Slam Winner (Modern).
Karrie Webb is a Women's Career Grand Slam Winner (Modern).
Annika Sörenstam is a Women's Career Grand Slam Winner (Modern).
Inbee Park is a Women's Career Grand Slam Winner (Modern).
